notes.subject: car
notes.text: The whole car is blurred, but a front-right antenna and a tiny bit of roof rack show; the neighbouring island group's car has no roof rack.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles are almost always concrete and often very thick; the neighbouring islands mostly have wooden ones.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs are green, while the neighbouring island group uses blue ones.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Tropical climate with dense, fairly low vegetation.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Roads often carry a very large number of road reflectors, as on the neighbouring islands.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs in Japanese, Chinese, Korean and even Russian are common because of tourism, also true next door.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Coverage is fairly limited, with almost nothing inland in the southern half.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Hills are mostly in the southern half, while the northern half is mostly flat.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Some signposts near the town of Apra View are yellow.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: A resort has white buildings with orange tiled roofs that superficially resemble roofs on Java.
